parties:
Asmatunnessa Khatun  ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Bangladesh ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment: 7. Law is very clear on the point, for satisfaction of the decree, law does not put any limitation to the attachment of movables and immovables of a judgment-debtor only subject to what is provided by section 60 of the Code of Civil Procedure. After attachment it is in the discretion of the executing Court to order for sale of so much of the attached property as would satisfy the claim of the decree. Prime focus expected of the execution Court is to promptly recover the decreed amount, particularly the compensation on account of acquisition of valuable property of a citizen. Failure over twelve years of the executing Court to realise the decreed amount is really very hard to believe.
